scope:
Exact-family representative350 receiver T(t), with conserved source heat.
Linear constant-property backing, chronological main-window schedule and finite
bulk storage. Prompt microsecond peaks are separate interval bounds, not dwell.

model.time_reference: Absolute dispatch focus times plus common R/c for prompt arrival; material arrival already references that clock.

prompt_interval_upper.interpretation: Conservative rectangular interval at the finite-depth Teff proxy peak. This interval is microseconds long; no peak is held through the material pulse. Radiation/thermal transfer remains a proxy.
prompt_interval_upper.short_time_scope: Until0.25s, upper history is min(finite-depth peak, wholepromptenergy surfaceimpulse at its finalemissiontime). Use this rather than linearly interpolating the coarse prompttail; the low-k surface bound is conservative for the finite100um skin.

limits: Heat-deposition curves conserve stage energy. Delayed heat is assigned its exponential radioactive time law without the larger envelope used for worst-case thermal bounds; full angular/relativistic arrival smearing is not solved.
All source heat is retained for this hot receiver history, a conservative reference rather than the coupled hot/cold capture partition.
The initial bulk offset is chosen to maintain minimum1000K during the finite archived schedule; startup heat and initial nonuniform state are explicit operating assumptions, not generated energy.

Nonuniform contributions older than20000s are omitted from the representative curves. The separate serialized-window thermal audit bounds total old tails/background corrections at about0.1K for350; add that bound when a strict upper curve is needed.
Microsecond prompt intervals are exported separately. The0.25s curves must not be used to infer an unresolved prompt temperature history.
The k4 skin is a quasi-steady resistance on the material/decay pulse; its millisecond transient, contact resistance and damaged-material kinetics are unresolved.
These are physical-model temperature histories for rate integration, not measured temperatures or a credible interval.
